behavior.arguments: rdi = base pointer. No argument is written except the two fields the window itself stores to.
behavior.distinction_from_packet_17: Packet #17 (0x15625e0) touches field +0x1a0 with a table-indexed OR rule (table[byte] OR into field+0x1a0). This window loads the pointer field [rdi+0x1a0] and clears the byte it points at when non-null, while storing 1 into a different field [rdi+0x108]. Same field offset, different rule and different struct role — no shared primitive claimed.

edges.non_null_pointer: Pointer field nonzero -> byte [pointer] cleared to 0, flag dword set to 1.
edges.null_pointer: Pointer field 0 -> je taken to ret; the byte clear is skipped, flag dword still set to 1.

behavior.entry_shape: Opens with endbr64; one forward branch, no calls: endbr64; mov 0x1a0(%rdi),%rax; movl $0x1,0x108(%rdi); test %rax,%rax; je 0x53cf57d; movb $0x0,(%rax); ret.
behavior.return_rule: No return value is claimed: on the null path rax is 0, on the clear path rax still holds the pointer. The observable effects are the flag store and the conditional byte clear, not a returned boolean.

coordinate_system: ELF virtual addresses, without a guessed loader or Ghidra rebase. The ELF section table maps .text with file offset = VA - 0x1000; the retained .eh_frame has equal file offset and VA. The tools resolve sections rather than assuming one global VA/file-offset relationship.

incoming_pattern_scan.note: Byte-pattern scan over the full .text section (70,370,352 bytes) for e8 sites whose rel32 lands on the window start; exactly seven sites found, each confirmed as an instruction start by linear disassembly from its caller FDE start. This is explicitly not a complete xref census: indirect calls, tail jumps, and PLT references are out of scope for the scan.
incoming_pattern_scan.relocation_note: No relocation record of any type in any .rela.* section names this window as addend (full-section scan: 80,022 .rela.dyn + 278 .rela.plt entries).
